facts: The Great Gatsby was released as a free eBook on January 17, 2021.
The eBook of The Great Gatsby is available at www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/64317.
The novel comprises nine chapters.
The eBook was produced by Alex Cabal for the Standard Ebooks project.
Nick Carraway moves to West Egg in 1922 to work in bonds.
Tom Buchanan has disturbing racial theories and a strained marriage with Daisy.
Daisy once wished her daughter would be "a beautiful little fool."
Nick observes Jay Gatsby standing alone on his lawn, gazing at a green light.
Tom Buchanan takes the narrator to meet his mistress Myrtle Wilson at her husband's garage.
Myrtle Wilson's sister Catherine and the McKees are among the guests at the Manhattan apartment.
Mr. McKee shows the narrator a portfolio of photographs titled "Beauty and the Beast," "Loneliness," "Old Grocery Horse," and "Brook'n Bridge."
The narrator ends up alone at Pennsylvania Station early in the morning.
The narrator attends one of Gatsby's extravagant parties at his Long Island mansion.
Owl Eyes crashes a new coupé into a ditch during the party.
The narrator works at a bond firm in New York City.
Jordan Baker is a famous golfer who has cheated in a golf tournament.
Jay Gatsby is a mysterious millionaire who hosts lavish parties.
Gatsby has been obsessed with Daisy Buchanan for five years.
Daisy married Tom Buchanan in a lavish ceremony.
Gatsby asks Nick to arrange a secret reunion with Daisy by inviting her to tea.
Nick arranges a tea meeting between Gatsby and Daisy at his West Egg house.
Gatsby sends a gardener and flowers in preparation for the meeting.
Daisy is moved to tears by Gatsby's beautiful shirts.
Nick exits into the rain, leaving Gatsby and Daisy alone together.
Gatsby was born James Gatz to poor farmers in North Dakota.
Gatsby met millionaire Dan Cody at the age of seventeen.
Gatsby inherited $25,000 after Dan Cody's death.
Daisy Buchanan found Gatsby's first party disappointingly vulgar.
Gatsby demands that Daisy leave Tom and declare her love for him.
Myrtle Wilson is struck and killed by Gatsby's yellow car.
Gatsby takes the blame for Myrtle's death to protect Daisy.
Nick finds Tom and Daisy sitting together in the kitchen.
The narrator visits Gatsby at dawn to warn him about suspicion surrounding his car.
Gatsby had a brief romance with Daisy during the war before she married Tom Buchanan.
Gatsby spent years building his fortune to reclaim Daisy.
Gatsby's body is discovered floating face-down in his pool.
Nick Carraway is responsible for arranging Gatsby's funeral.
Catherine testifies falsely to protect Daisy's reputation.
Gatsby's father comes from Minnesota to attend the funeral.
Tom reveals the car's ownership to Wilson, leading to Gatsby's death.
